author: Donovan Varney
title: Boone County flood relief underway after heavy rainfall - NewsBreak
text:
By Donovan Varney ,
1 days ago
BOONE COUNTY, W.Va. (WOWK) — Relief efforts are underway after heavy rainfall caused significant flood damage in Boone County.
A meeting was held Tuesday morning with members of the Boone County Commission, Sheriff’s Office, Emergency Management Agency and National Guard.
W.Va. Latest News:
According to Boone County Sheriff Chad Barker, the areas that were hit the hardest were off of Route 85 and Route 17.
“Water rescue teams came in. We have some in Boone, also in Kanawha County,” Barker said. “We were able to get some people out of their homes.”
While Barker reported no injuries or casualties, many homes and buildings suffered damage.
“Some people were in medical need, so we were able to get those people out,” Barker said. “People were panicking. You know, water coming up around their homes and we were able to rescue them as well.”
Pond Fork is a tributary of the Little Coal River that runs through Boone County. The tributary dumped off water and debris into many nearby communities, including Van and Wharton. One Van resident said the water wrapped around her whole house and flooded the basement.
Freedie Freewill Baptist Church is located right alongside Pond Fork in Van. The church’s basement, which holds Sunday School classes, was about a foot deep in water, residents said.
Kim Lusk and her husband arrived early Tuesday morning with equipment to help clear the parking lot and basement.
“It’s a mess to clean up,” Lusk said. “You know, we’ve had it happen before… We understand it.”
Lusk said she is grateful to be able to lend a hand at the church since so many of the people that attend it are elders.
In addition to people like Lusk helping out, the American Red Cross was stationed at the Van Volunteer Fire Department on Tuesday to offer aid. A representative of the Red Cross said the damage wasn’t severe enough for many residents to need the Red Crosses assistance, so he only expects to be there a day.
While members of the community have come together to help clean up flood debris, Boone County Commissioner Jeff Petry said the recovery efforts may last a while.
“This happened overnight. It was an eight hour event, but it’s going to take more than eight days. It’ll probably take more like eight weeks or possibly eight months,” Petry said.
The Boone County Emergency Management Agency urges people to call 304-369-7273 if they need further assistance. To report any damages from the floods, visit www.boonewv.com .
